name: Session
hook: Privacy-first messenger with onion routing and no phone number required.
bullets: No phone number or email required to sign up or message
End-to-end encrypted by default with Signal Protocol
Onion routing (Lokinet) protects IP and metadata
benefits: Communicate without tying your identity to a phone number
Stronger metadata protection than traditional E2E messengers
Free, open-source, and not monetized by ads or data harvesting
Works across mobile, desktop, and web
setupSteps: Install Session from getsession.org, F-Droid, or your app store
Create a Session ID (no phone number or email required)
Add contacts by sharing your Session ID or scanning a QR code
Start messaging with E2E encryption and onion routing
details: Session is a free, open-source, end-to-end encrypted messenger that minimizes metadata exposure. Unlike most messengers, Session doesn't require a phone number or email to create an account — instead you get a random Session ID. Messages use the Signal Protocol for E2E encryption, and Session routes traffic through an onion-routing network (Lokinet) to hide your IP address and reduce metadata. It's cross-platform (Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, Linux), open-source, and designed with decentralization in mind. Session is a great privacy-focused alternative to Signal, WhatsApp, and Telegram for users who want minimal identity exposure and stronger metadata protection.
